title: Do not leave pieces free

card.idea: The habit runs both ways. After you pick a move, ask one question: can anything of mine be taken for free now? A piece you leave hanging is a gift.
card.habit: Take hanging pieces, never hang your own.

explain.text: Both white pieces are hanging. The rook on c7 attacks the knight on c4, and the bishop on g7 attacks the bishop on d4. Neither white piece has a defender.
Before you play a move, look at the square you are moving to. The bishop would love c4, but the pawn on b5 covers it, so the bishop would simply be taken.

challenges.prompt: You want to play the bishop to c4. Is that safe?
reasons: Yes, no black piece can reach c4.
No, the pawn on b5 takes it.
No, the king on e8 takes it.

challenges.prompt: The rook takes on d8. Is that a fair deal?
reasons: No, the rook is simply lost.
Yes, the knight on b7 takes back but a rook for a rook is even.
No, the king on f7 takes back.

challenges.prompt: Tap every white piece that is hanging right now.
Black left something free. Take it.
challenges.reason: The bishop on b8 is attacked and undefended.

wrong.Rxd5: The rook on d5 is worth 5, but the queen on f7 is free and worth 9.

challenges.reason: The queen on f7 is hanging, so the rook takes it.

challenges.prompt: Pawn wars: get a pawn to the far side before your opponent does.

takeaway: Before you move, check nothing of yours is left hanging.
